([[Lincolnshire, Illinois]]) | college = * [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] (2017–2020) * [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] (2020–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = [[2021-22 NBA G League season|2021–2022]] | team1 = [[Raptors 905]] | years2 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022–2023]] | team2 = [[Delaware Blue Coats]] | years3 = 2023–2024 | team3 = [[Hapoel Holon B.C.|Hapoel Holon]] | years4 = 2024–2026 | team4 = [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C|Hapoel Jerusalem]] | years5 = 2026–present | team5 = [[KK Budućnost|Budućnost]] | highlights = * [[List of NBA G League champions|NBA G League champion]] ([[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]]) }} '''Justin Smith''' (born March 1, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[KK Budućnost|Budućnost]] of the Montenegrin [[Prva A Liga]], the [[ABA League]], and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]] and the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]]. ==High school career== [[File:20150321 IHSA Class 4A championship game Justin Smith jumper.jpg|left|thumb|Smith during 2015 [[Illinois High School Association|IHSA]] Class 4A championship game]] Smith attended [[Stevenson High School (Lincolnshire, Illinois)|Stevenson High School]] in [[Lincolnshire, Illinois]]. In his sophomore season, he played alongside [[Jalen Brunson]] and won the 2015 [[Illinois High School Association|IHSA]] Class 4A state title.{{cite web |last1=Narang |first1=Bob |title=Stevenson's Justin Smith looked up to teammates before choosing Indiana |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/buffalo-grove/sports/ct-lsr-stevenson-basketball-justin-smith-indiana-tl-1006-20160929-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=March 5, 2021 |date=September 29, 2016}} As a senior, Smith averaged 21.7 points and 10 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Shalin |first1=Dan |title=All-Area Boys Basketball First Team: Justin Smith, Stevenson |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/buffalo-grove/sports/ct-lsr-justin-smith-basketball-first-team-all-area-tl-0330-20170329-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=March 5, 2021 |date=March 29, 2017}} A consensus four-star recruit, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] over offers from [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]] and [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]].{{cite web |last1=Helfgot |first1=Mike |title=Stevenson basketball standout Justin Smith commits to Indiana |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/post-tribune/sports/ct-lns-boys-basketball-stevenson-justin-smith-indiana-st-0928-20160927-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=March 5, 2021 |date=September 27, 2016}} ==College career== As a freshman at Indiana, Smith averaged 6.5 points and 3.2 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Narang |first1=Bob |title=Hoosier hops: Stevenson grad Justin Smith putting on a show at Indiana |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/lincolnshire/sports/ct-lsr-justin-smith-indiana-hoosiers-update-tl-0920-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=March 5, 2021 |date=September 17, 2018}} On March 2, 2019, he scored a sophomore season-high 24 points in a 63–62 upset win over sixth-ranked [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]].{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Tim |title=No. 6 MSU Upset by Unranked Indiana; Justin Smith Drops 24 Points |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2823188-no-6-msu-upset-by-unranked-indiana-justin-smith-drops-24-points |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=March 5, 2021 |date=March 2, 2019}} Smith averaged 8.2 points and 4.5 rebounds per game as a sophomore, his first year in a starting role.{{cite web |last1=Flaherty |first1=Kevin |title=Watch: Justin Smith attacks rim with posterizing dunks |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Indiana-Hoosiers-basketball-Justin-Smith-poster-dunks-138274870/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=March 5, 2021 |date=November 9, 2019}} In his junior season, he averaged 10.4 points and 5.2 rebounds per game, before leaving the program.{{cite web |last1=Osterman |first1=Zach |title=Insider: IU has the pieces to replace forward Justin Smith, who will graduate and transfer |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2020/05/22/indiana-basketball-justin-smith-graduate-transfer/5243741002/ |website=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |access-date=March 5, 2021 |date=May 22, 2020}} Smith moved to [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] as a graduate transfer.{{cite magazine |last1=Brew |first1=Tom |title=Former Indiana Forward Justin Smith Transferring to Arkansas |url=https://www.si.com/college/indiana/basketball/former-indiana-justin-smith-transfer-arkansas |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=March 5, 2021 |date=June 8, 2020}} On December 20, 2020, he recorded 22 points and 17 rebounds in an 87–76 victory over [[Oral Roberts Golden Eagles men's basketball|Oral Roberts]].{{cite web |last1=Bordelon |first1=Scottie |title=Smith 'remarkable' in Hogs' win over ORU |url=https://www.wholehogsports.com/news/2020/dec/20/smith-remarkable-hogs-win-over-oru/ |website=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |access-date=March 5, 2021 |date=December 20, 2020}} Smith missed four games with an ankle injury that required surgery.{{cite web |last1=Allen |first1=Nate |title=Smith's return a major boon for Hogs |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2021/feb/20/smiths-return-a-major-boon-for-hogs/ |website=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |access-date=March 5, 2021 |date=February 20, 2021}} As a senior, he averaged 13.6 points and 7.3 rebounds per game, helping lead the Razorbacks to a 25–7 record and a berth in the Elite Eight of the NCAA Tournament. Following the season, Smith declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Muck |first1=Jeremy |title=STATE SPORTS BRIEFS: Smith to declare for draft, sign with agent |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2021/may/03/state-sports-briefs/ |access-date=October 3, 2021 |work=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |date=May 3, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Raptors 905 (2021–2022)=== On December 31, 2021, Smith was acquired via waivers by the [[Raptors 905]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He was waived on February 7, 2022.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|date=December 31, 2021|access-date=February 10, 2022}} On February 10, 2022, Smith was reacquired and activated by the [[Raptors 905]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=February 10, 2022|access-date=February 10, 2022}} In 29 games in 2021-22 he averaged 8.5 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 0.7 blocks per game, while shooting 57.1% from the field. ===Delaware Blue Coats (2022–2023)=== On November 4, 2022, Smith was named to the opening night roster for the [[Delaware Blue Coats]]{{cite web|title=Blue Coats Announce Opening Night Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/blue-coats-announce-opening-night-roster/n-5895485|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}} and eventually helped the team win the [[NBA G League]] title.{{cite web|first=Noah|last=Levick|title=Delaware Blue Coats win G League championship; Jaden Springer named Finals MVP|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/sixers/delaware-blue-coats-nba-g-league-championship-2023-jaden-springer-mac-mcclung|website=NBCSports.com|date=April 7, 2023|access-date=April 7, 2023}} In 45 games in 2022-23 he averaged 9.6 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 0.6 blocks per game, while shooting 55.7% from the field. ===Hapoel Holon (2023–2024)=== On July 23, 2023, Smith signed with [[Hapoel Holon B.C.|Hapoel Holon]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{cite web|first=Dario|last=Skerletic|title=Justin Smith joins Hapoel Holon|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/justin-smith-joins-hapoel-holon/|website=Sportando.basketball|date=July 23, 2023|access-date=July 24, 2023}} In 38 games in 2023-24 he averaged 16.0 points, 6.5 rebounds, and 0.9 blocks per game, while shooting 62.7% from the field.[https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Justin-Smith/Summary/88895 "Justin Smith Player Profile,"] realgm. On June 13, 2024, Smith was drafted by the [[Valley Suns]] in the [[2024 NBA G League expansion draft]].{{cite web|title=2024-25 NBA G League Expansion Draft|url=https://gleague.nba.com/2024-expansion-draft|website=NBA.com|date=June 13, 2024|access-date=June 14, 2024}} ===Hapoel Jerusalem (2024–2026)=== On July 4, 2024, he signed with [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/hapoel-jerusalem-signs-justin-smith-until-2026/|title=Hapoel Jerusalem signs Justin Smith until 2026|last=|first=|date=July 4, 2024|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 4, 2024}} In 40 games in 2024-25 he averaged 11.7 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 0.7 blocks per game, while shooting 63.5% from the field. ===Budućnost (2026–present)=== On July 7, 2026, Smith signed a one-year deal with [[KK Budućnost|Budućnost]] of the Montenegrin [[Prva A Liga]], the [[ABA League]], and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].{{cite web|title=Buducnost brings in forward Justin Smith|url=https://staging.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/eurocup/news/buducnost-brings-in-forward-justin-smith/|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|date=July 7, 2026|accessdate=August 4, 2026}} ==Career
